title: J.D.B. v. North Carolina (2011)
key_points: Holding: A child's age, when known or objectively apparent, is relevant to whether he is in custody for Miranda purposes.
officer_notes: Scenario: You question a 13-year-old in a closed school conference room about thefts.
Takeaway: With juveniles, assume custody sooner and follow juvenile interrogation rules, including parent notification policies.
